beats.vo: Hi. I am Anton.
beats.bullet: Anton Gulda — founder

beats.vo: I work rotational shifts at an oil field, two weeks away from home at a time.
beats.bullet: Rotational shifts at an oil field

beats.vo: On my rotations off, I build verification infrastructure for the physical world, on Solana.
beats.bullet: On rotations off: building on Solana

beats.vo: Every number that reaches a market starts as a claim somebody typed.
beats.bullet: A kilowatt-hour, a carbon credit, an ESG report

beats.vo: A spreadsheet cell can be edited. A portal can be inflated.
beats.bullet: Spreadsheets can be edited

beats.vo: And the same megawatt-hour can be sold twice.
beats.bullet: The same MWh can be sold twice

beats.vo: Markets move in milliseconds, while verification still runs on annual audits.
beats.bullet: Verification still runs on annual audits

beats.vo: The result has a name: greenwashing.
beats.bullet: The result has a name

scenes.label: 03 / 06   THE SOLUTION
scenes.headline: Axis Protocol — an open standard for trust

beats.vo: Axis Protocol closes that gap: identity, proof, attestation, policy.
beats.bullet: Identity · Proof · Attestation · Policy

beats.vo: Every reading is signed on the device with Ed25519 — at the tier mainnet requires, that key lives inside an NXP SE050 and never leaves the chip, and the build refuses to compile without it.
beats.bullet: Ed25519 on the device · mainnet build requires SE050

beats.vo: Then at least two staked oracles vote on the same canonical hash.
beats.bullet: At least two staked oracles — separate keys

beats.vo: A contradictory vote is a slashing event, and minting waits for a finalised attestation.
beats.bullet: Contradiction = slashing; mint waits for finalisation

beats.vo: One compromised oracle cannot create value.
beats.bullet: One compromised oracle cannot create value

scenes.label: 04 / 06   WHAT IS DONE
scenes.headline: Not a slide deck — it runs

beats.vo: Fifty-eight on-chain instructions in Rust.
beats.bullet: 58 on-chain instructions

beats.vo: Two hundred and seventy-six tests pass: Rust, Node, Python and Foundry.
beats.bullet: 276 tests green

beats.vo: The protocol is live on devnet today — two staked oracle instances, and a mint that only passed because the quorum was finalised.
beats.bullet: Live on devnet — 2 staked oracle instances

beats.vo: A finalised attestation, and a mint that only executed because the gate said required equals true.
beats.bullet: Finalised attestation, then mint through the gate

beats.vo: Every proof and mint is public — verify it yourself.
beats.bullet: Every proof and mint is public — verify it yourself

beats.vo: Why me? I have no degree, no team and no funding.
beats.bullet: No degree · no team · no funding

beats.vo: Four months of nights and rotations off. I wrote the firmware, the contracts, the oracles and the AI layer myself.
beats.bullet: Firmware, contracts, oracles, AI — one person

beats.vo: I got tired of watching physical data be trusted on faith.
beats.bullet: Tired of physical data trusted on faith

beats.vo: This is not a sprint for me. It is a mission: make the physical world provable. Judge me by the code, not by the pitch.
beats.bullet: A mission, not a sprint — judge me by the code

beats.vo: So here is my ask. I need one real pilot: a solar site, a meter, an operator — anyone whose data should be provable.
beats.bullet: A real site with a meter — solar, wind, or a lab bench

beats.vo: And I need mentors who have taken infrastructure like this to mainnet.
beats.bullet: Mentors who took infrastructure to mainnet

beats.vo: The protocol is open, the devnet is live, and the code is public.
beats.bullet: Open protocol · live devnet · public code

beats.vo: If that is you, let us talk.
beats.bullet: github.com/AntonGrid/ENRG
